title: Plaguelands: The Scarlet Enclave
body: In the far southeastern corner of the Plaguelands, beyond the reach of the blight, the Scarlet Crusade built a haven it called the Scarlet Enclave. Its towns are clean and whole: the farms, mine, mill and stables of Havenshire, the walled town of New Avalon with its hold, chapel and town hall, and ships riding at anchor off the coast. Then a necropolis appeared in the sky. Acherus, the Ebon Hold, has come to rest above the Enclave, and from it the Lich King looses his newest weapon, the death knights, under Highlord Darion Mograine. From the plateau of Death's Breach below the hold they ride against the Crusade, and beyond the hills to the west stands Light's Hope Chapel, the Argent Dawn's stronghold, which the Lich King calls a blemish upon the Plaguelands.

The last Scarlet armies to arrive died beneath the necropolis, and the Lich King turned his knights west against Light's Hope Chapel.

title: Acherus: The Ebon Hold
body: Acherus is a necropolis raised as the citadel of the Lich King's death knights, and its masters boast that not even Naxxramas could withstand an assault from it. Its design is credited to Obrahiim the Traveler, who also helped conceive Naxxramas. In the Heart of Acherus on the upper floor, Instructor Razuvious measures freshly raised knights, runeforges glow for the etching of blades, and the unworthy hang in chains to be killed. Below lies the Hall of Command, where Highlord Mograine keeps his command post and the masters of blood, frost and unholy teach. Through its great eye the Lich King sees deep into enemy land.

title: Death's Breach
body: Death's Breach is the plateau beneath the floating Ebon Hold, the staging ground for the Scourge's assault on the Enclave. Scourge gryphons carry knights down from Acherus to a camp of tents, roosts and runeforges, where Prince Valanar drives the assault and Salanar the Horseman, Gothik the Harvester and Orithos the Sky Darkener each claim new blood for their tasks. Here too Olrun the Battlecaller sets initiates to duel one another in Death's Challenge, a rite said to be born of the Lich King's victory over Illidan.

title: Havenshire
body: Havenshire is the working heart of the Enclave, a farming town of fields, pumpkin patches and a lumber mill north of New Avalon's walls, its people Scarlet peasants and citizens who feed and supply the Crusade. It is the first place the death knights strike. Prince Valanar wants the fleeing villagers killed above all, to plant terror, and the Sky Darkeners loose saronite arrows at anyone running for the safety of New Avalon, while crusaders make their stand to save the horses, mines, lumber and people of the town.

Salanar the Horseman sends initiates to steal a steed from under the guards, then has his dark riders slay and raise the beasts as deathchargers in the Realm of Shadows. The stablemaster, Kitrik, has sent more than one horse thief back to the Lich King in pieces. In the stables lies the diary of an unknown crusader, who watched a necropolis darken the bright morning and drew up a map for swimming all the way round the coast to Tirisfal.

With the Scourge at its door, the Crusade is trying to strip the mine bare and save what it can, and its miners haul every load they can toward the frigates at anchor off Light's Point. Gothik the Harvester, grand necromancer of the Lich King, has taken an interest in the place. He has a gift for the Scarlet miners, one he promises will speed up their work: a portable plague spreader.

With the Scourge loose in Havenshire, the Crusade has thrown every soldier it has outside New Avalon into a blockade here, guarding the frigates while ore from the mine is loaded aboard. Cannons line the shore, and a thousand defenders stand between the Scourge and the ships.

title: New Avalon
body: New Avalon is the last bastion of the Scarlet Crusade in the Enclave, a walled town of orchards, an inn, a forge, a great hold, a chapel and a town hall. Its people were promised safety. As Havenshire's survivors crowd in, High General Abbendis, with High Abbot Landgren alongside, tells them that only the pure of heart will be allowed to stay, and the inquisitors will turn the rest away. Ghouls hammer at the gates, and frightened citizens beg to know where the last ships are going. Even its inn and forge draw the Scourge's eye, for Noth the Plaguebringer wants a cauldron and chains for his plague.

In the last days a furious crowd besieges it, shouting that they were promised safety and demanding to know what the Crimson Dawn is and where the ships are bound. Within, councilmen keep to their posts, and the town registry records the births, deaths and comings and goings of the Crusade's people. Prince Keleseth wants no official left alive.

Scarlet Commander Rodrick and his soldiers keep its halls, and its alarms are quick to sound at the first sign of intruders.

Death knights sent behind the lines to hunt a Scarlet courier have made it their hideout, and Orbaz Bloodbane and Thassarian run their part of the war from its common room, Scarlet corpses strewn across the floor. None of the crusaders they questioned could say when or where the courier would come, so Orbaz plots to steal the patrol schedule from the Scarlet Hold and find out for himself.

It is one of the four Scarlet fortifications in New Avalon, with the forge, the town hall and the hold, that the eye of Acherus was sent to study before the assault. Behind its holy work lies a prison house where the inquisitors hold their captives.

body: Instructor Razuvious, a master of Naxxramas, oversees the making of new death knights in the Heart of Acherus. He judges each body the necromancers raise: a champion is sent to the Lich King, a failure who wakes with emotion and memory intact is disposed of. He sets each initiate to forge a first runeblade, teaches runeforging, and hands over the key that frees an unworthy prisoner to be killed in cold blood, for only then does the endless hunger ease. His word on desertion is posted in the frontline reports: any death knight who deserts will suffer without end, and he will see to it himself.

At Death's Breach he receives the knights Valanar sends him with a gift for the Crusade: a portable plague spreader, meant for the Scarlet miners in Havenshire. He has saved a special place for its victims in what he calls his vacuum cleaner of souls.

title: Lord Thorval
body: Lord Thorval, master of the school of blood in the Hall of Command, was once a paladin who left his wife and two daughters at home to hunt the Scourge. He came back to find his village burned and his family dead behind a barred door, killed by the Scarlet Crusade on a rumor of plague. Broken by grief and rage, he was overrun by the very Scourge he had hunted, and swore himself to the Lich King as the blows fell. His memoirs, left for new knights troubled by their past, praise the Scourge for purging the feelings that tormented him. Every mortal story, he writes, ends the same way: in death.

title: In Service of the Lich King
body: Every death knight of Acherus begins the same way: raised by necromancers in the Heart of Acherus and measured by Instructor Razuvious. Those found worthy are sent to the Lich King, who gives them immortality and a purpose, to bring doom to the Scarlet Crusade and to Light's Hope below. Each initiate takes a battle-worn sword from the racks and forges it into a runeblade, learns to etch runes of power upon it, and then is handed a key. Chained nearby are the unworthy, fellow risen who woke with too much of their old selves. One is freed, armed and fought to the death, and the hunger fades.

Prince Valanar wants terror first: crusaders slain and left for the death march, and above all the fleeing villagers, because killing them is what breaks the hearts of men. Salanar the Horseman has them steal horses from the stables to be remade as deathchargers, Orithos's Sky Darkeners rain saronite arrows on the roads, and Gothik the Harvester waits with a gift for the miners while the Crusade strips the Havenshire Mine and loads its frigates at Light's Point.

title: The Crimson Dawn
body: With New Avalon under siege, Prince Keleseth decides that a few hundred mindless ghouls at the gate will not do. The town's officials must die to show that none escape the Scourge, so he sends a knight into the town hall to kill Mayor Quimby and bring back the New Avalon registry. Outside the hall a furious crowd is already pounding on the doors, crying that they were promised safety and demanding to know where the last ships are going, and what the Crimson Dawn might be.

Plaguefist saved the few still breathing for the knights to execute, and he picked one out for each of them in particular, a feisty prisoner of the knight's own race. It was no accident whom they found, and Plaguefist is sure each knight will relish the kill.

body: With the Enclave in ashes, the Lich King gives his last command: Light's Hope Chapel must fall. His knights pass through the Noxious Glade to Browman Mill, where Scourge Commander Thalanor waits and Darion Mograine is to give the final march orders. The Argent Dawn stands defiant at the chapel, and the knights are promised that this day they ascend into the immortal realm of Scourge heroes. Darion calls the Scourge to rise, and thousands of the dead march on the chapel with the knights of Acherus at their head. The defense of the chapel is told among the tales of the Eastern Plaguelands.
